title: OpenType Features, Glyph Browser & Text Styles Hierarchy
subtitle: Ligatures, Stylistic Alternates, Swashes & Paragraph/Character Styles

learningObjectives: Use the OpenType controls available from the text Context Toolbar to apply font-supported typographic features.
Activate and manage Standard Ligatures, Discretionary Ligatures, Contextual Alternates, and Swash flourishes.
Use the Glyph Browser panel to browse and insert Unicode characters and font-specific alternate glyphs.
Build a reusable hierarchy of paragraph and character styles; confirm the current style-creation UI in the target build.
Understand character-level style overrides versus paragraph-level structural formatting.
standardSections.foundationalKnowledge: Modern professional typography uses OpenType features, including standard and discretionary ligatures, stylistic alternates and swashes. Affinity exposes OpenType features from the text Context Toolbar, with the available options depending on the selected font. The Glyph Browser panel lets you insert Unicode characters and font-specific alternates: create a text insertion point, open Window > Text > Glyph Browser, choose the font family, style and subset, then double-click a glyph. Affinity supports reusable paragraph and character styles; the exact current UI location for creating and managing them should be verified on the target build.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Select text and inspect OpenType controls
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Select an Artistic Text or Frame Text object. Inspect the text Context Toolbar for OpenType controls available to the selected font. The available feature options vary by font.

stepByStepInstructions.title: Apply font-supported ligatures
stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Use the OpenType controls in the text Context Toolbar to enable Standard Ligatures and, where the font supports them, Discretionary Ligatures. Compare the rendering and keep decorative ligatures for display text when appropriate.

stepByStepInstructions.instruction: Create a text insertion point. From the Window menu, open Text > Glyph Browser. Choose the font family, font style and subset from the available menus, then double-click a glyph to insert it. Available glyphs depend on the selected font.

commonPitfalls.pitfall: OpenType features button is grayed out or has no effect
commonPitfalls.cause: The active font does not contain OpenType font tables for that feature (many cheap or web-ripped fonts lack ligatures and swashes).
commonPitfalls.solution: Switch to an authentic OpenType font (e.g. Adobe Garamond, Playfair Display, Montserrat, or Cormorant Garamond).

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Accidentally styling whole paragraph when trying to format one word
commonPitfalls.cause: Applying a Paragraph Style instead of a Character Style to a localized selection.
commonPitfalls.solution: Use Paragraph Styles for whole-block formatting (margins, leading); use Character Styles for inline word accents (bold, color, swash).

commonPitfalls.pitfall: Manual overrides overriding global Text Style updates
commonPitfalls.cause: Editing point size manually after applying a text style adds a '+' override badge.
commonPitfalls.solution: Click the 'Clear Overrides' button in the Text Styles panel to re-synchronize the text with its master style definition.

options: Use the Layers panel to convert text into curves.
Place a text insertion point, open Window > Text > Glyph Browser, choose a font/style/subset and double-click a glyph.
Open the Symbols panel and select a symbol.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The current Help Center instructions are to create an insertion point, open Window > Text > Glyph Browser, choose the font family, style and subset, then double-click the glyph.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the difference between 'Standard Ligatures' and 'Discretionary Ligatures'?
options: Standard ligatures are free; discretionary ligatures cost money.
Standard ligatures fix physical character collisions for readability (fi, fl, ffi); Discretionary ligatures are decorative or historical joints (st, ct) used for artistic styling.
Standard ligatures only work in English; Discretionary ligatures work in French.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Standard ligatures resolve optical collisions to improve body copy legibility, whereas Discretionary ligatures add stylistic, historical, or vintage flair.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why use reusable paragraph and character styles instead of formatting every text frame manually?
options: They prevent users from changing words.
They let related text keep consistent formatting and make later style changes easier to apply consistently.
They remove all text from the document.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Affinity supports reusable paragraph and character styles to maintain consistency across text in a design.

slides.title: OpenType Features, Glyph Browser & Text Styles Hierarchy
slides.subtitle: Unlocking Hidden Font Treasures & Enterprise Style Systems
slides.contentMarkdown: Welcome to **Lesson D06-03**. In this lesson, use the text Context Toolbar to explore font-supported OpenType features, the **Glyph Browser panel** to insert Unicode and alternate glyphs, and reusable paragraph and character styles to maintain typographic consistency.

actionBox.label: Typography Superpower
actionBox.text: Turn ordinary typing into bespoke hand-lettered art using OpenType swashes and alternates.

slides.title: The World of OpenType Features
slides.subtitle: Ligatures, Swashes & Stylistic Sets
slides.contentMarkdown:
Professional OpenType fonts are mini software programs packed with features:

1. **Standard Ligatures (`liga`):** Eliminates collisions where letter dots hit crossbars (e.g. `fi`, `fl`, `ffi`).
2. **Discretionary Ligatures (`dlig`):** Vintage artistic bridges (e.g. `ct`, `st`, `sp`).
3. **Swashes (`swsh`):** Extends calligraphic flourish tails on capital letters.
4. **Stylistic Sets (`ss01-20`):** Alternate letter cuts (e.g. swapping between a geometric circular 'a' and a humanist double-story 'a').

visual.content: Standard Ligatures (fi, fl) | Discretionary (st, ct) | Swashes (Flourishes) | Stylistic Sets

slides.title: OpenType controls in the text Context Toolbar
slides.subtitle: Your Control Center for Font Features
slides.contentMarkdown:
Select a text object and inspect the **Context Toolbar** for OpenType controls supported by the selected font.

- **Ligatures:** standard and discretionary ligatures where included in the font.
- **Stylistic alternates and swashes:** available only when the font contains those glyphs.
- **Font dependency:** the exact features shown vary by typeface.

actionBox.label: Quality Note
actionBox.text: OpenType features require a font that contains them! Quality typefaces (Playfair, Baskerville, Montserrat) shine here.

slides.title: The Glyph Browser panel
slides.subtitle: Discovering Every Embedded Character
slides.contentMarkdown:
Open the panel using `Window > Text > Glyph Browser`.

1. Create a text insertion point.
2. Choose the font family, style and subset from the panel menus.
3. Double-click a glyph to insert it at the insertion point.

Available characters and alternates depend on the selected font.

visual.content: Text insertion point → Window > Text > Glyph Browser → choose font family/style/subset → double-click glyph

slides.title: Paragraph Styles vs Character Styles
slides.subtitle: The Two Pillars of Text Architecture
slides.contentMarkdown:
Affinity supports reusable **paragraph styles** and **character styles**.

- Paragraph styles apply consistent formatting to paragraph-level text.
- Character styles apply consistent formatting to selected characters or runs of text.
- The exact current menu/panel location for creating, updating and clearing style overrides should be checked on the target build.

visual.content: Paragraph Style: Formats entire block structure VS Character Style: Formats inline words/accents

slides.subtitle: Building Design System Typography Tokens

actionBox.label: Design Token Power

slides.title: OpenType & Style Pitfalls
slides.subtitle: Avoid Common Typography Bugs
slides.contentMarkdown:
### 1. Font lacks a requested OpenType feature
- **Check:** The selected font may not include a particular ligature, swash or alternate glyph.
- **Approach:** Choose a font that includes the required feature and inspect the text Context Toolbar again.

### 2. Glyph not available
- **Check:** Glyph availability depends on the selected font family, style and subset.
- **Approach:** Choose the correct font/style/subset in Glyph Browser before inserting.

### 3. Style-management control differs
- **Check:** The exact current style-creation and override controls are not verified in this review.
- **Approach:** Confirm the target-build UI before following a documented menu path.

visual.content: Clear Overrides to Re-Sync | Discretionary for Titles Only | Standard Ligatures for Body

slides.title: Independent Challenge: Historical Book Title Page
slides.subtitle: Put OpenType & Text Styles to the Test
slides.contentMarkdown:
### Your Mission:
Construct a literary title page:
1. Use a serif font with Discretionary Ligatures where supported.
2. Open Window > Text > Glyph Browser and insert an available alternate or swash glyph.
3. Use OpenType Small Caps if the chosen font supports it.
4. Create reusable paragraph and character styles for the title, author and metadata.

### Acceptance Criteria:
- Supported OpenType features appear correctly.
- Glyph Browser used to insert an available alternate character.
- Paragraph and character styles maintain consistent formatting.
